TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Palawan
DATE 16 November 2028 · 1000 local
SIDE Philippine Navy
WINDOW 110 min, closes at 165
Tarlac class landing platform dock. Photo: U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class Daniel B... · CC BY-SA 4.0 · cropped
"Victory smiles upon those who anticipate the changes in the character of war, not upon those who wait to adapt themselves after the changes occur."
- Giulio Douhet, 1921

OFF ABORLAN, 1000. Two nights ago a Meridian landing craft put two truck-mounted Silkworm launchers ashore on the Aborlan coast, thirty miles south of Puerto Princesa, with a fire-control radar and two anti-aircraft guns. Yesterday the battery fired on a coaster off Narra and missed. Nothing has sailed for Balabac since.

The launchers reach about twenty-five miles. Your ships are thirty-eight miles south of them, outside that range, and the Balabac convoy is held at the Narra anchorage, twenty miles from them and inside their reach.

Destroy both launchers. A 76 mm gun reaches them from eight miles; a helicopter or an FA-50 from wherever the guns let it. The battery has kept under cover with its radar off since it fired yesterday; expect it up within about five minutes, and then it will fire at what its radar finds, the convoy included. Every round you fire comes back only from a supply ship, and this is the last window that sells them.
COMMAND NET: A mission-specific tactical report follows eight minutes after the start. It is advice from the command team, not a new sensor detection.

FORWARD RECON: MOTH 11, a small RQ-7 reconnaissance UAV, joins over the local approach at minute ten, allowing time for initial air-defence suppression. The field team uses a portable launcher and local recovery lane. Two reserve UAVs are with the team from the start. They are unarmed and have finite fuel. Use their sensors to classify the military installations and update strike aimpoints. The small airframes are vulnerable; no scripted reveal grants a target solution. Keep a recovery margin and reposition the initial track as needed.
Naval Forces West
COMMANDER'S INTENT

Both launchers destroyed opens the road. The radar and the guns are there to make that expensive; they do not have to be destroyed. Run in fast, or blind them first, or let the FA-50s go in - but the convoy at the anchorage is inside the launchers' range too, and it has to be there when you are done.
• Destroy both Silkworm launchers
• Keep the Balabac convoy afloat
• Keep the lead ship afloat
• Destroy the fire-control radar
• Harm no banca
• Obtain a current classification of the land target area

Your task group, its aircraft and any supply ships you own. At the anchorage: the Balabac convoy and, if she survived the rendezvous, MV Sulu Provider. Ashore: two Silkworm launchers, a fire-control radar, two anti-aircraft guns. Neutral: bancas. Forward RQ-7 field team: two reserve UAVs and a portable launcher; Moth 11 joins at minute ten.

The planned window is 110 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 55 minutes more; the operation is closed at 165 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
